headline: Introduced homestead tax exemption ordinance; recommended $156,000 sale of Lot #6 Southeast Business Park; approved Edgewood Pre-K contract amendment.
summary: A proposed homestead property tax exemption would exempt between 5% and 35% of the assessed value of owner-occupied homes, with a public hearing set for December 1. A letter asks the Zoning Commission to speed up a zoning change that would remove the Data Center Special Permit use. The city will pay $107,135.48 net to settle a workers' compensation case.

transcript:
The regular meeting of the City Council was held on Tuesday, November 10, 2026 in the City Hall Council Chambers, 111 North Main Street at 7:06 p.m. Present: Mayor Zoppo-Sassu; Council Members Dickau, Hahn, Kelley, Rosengren, Seymour and Tyler.

# 1. CALL TO ORDER

# 2. APPROVAL OF MINUTES

On motion of Council Member Hahn and seconded by Council Member Dickau, it was unanimously voted: To approve the minutes of the Red Light Traffic Camera Forum held on October 6, 2026.

On motion of Council Member Rosengren and seconded by Council Member Dickau, it was unanimously voted: To approve the minutes of the regular City Council meeting held on October 13, 2026.

On motion of Council Member Dickau and seconded by Council Member Seymour, it was unanimously voted: To approve the minutes of the special City Council meeting held on October 29, 2026.

# 3. PUBLIC PARTICIPATION

Mary Ann Sirois, 362 Shrub Road – Ms. Sirois spoke in opposition to the Homestead Act Tax Exemption. She stated that the exemption shifts the tax burden from one set of property owners to another.

# 4. ANNOUNCEMENTS

Council members reported on committees, activities, and events.

# 5. ADOPTION OF CONSENT CALENDAR

On motion of Council Member Hahn and seconded by Council Member Tyler, it was unanimously voted: To adopt the Consent Agenda with the exception of item g.

## a. New Hire Report for October 2026

Communication received from the Human Resources Department.

As part of the Consent Calendar adoption and on motion of Council Member Hahn and seconded, it was unanimously voted: To place on file the New Hire Report for the month of October, 2026.

## b. Tax Refunds in the Amount of $23,538.62

Request presented from Tax Collector Bednaz.

As part of the Consent Calendar adoption and on motion of Council Member Hahn and seconded, it was unanimously voted: To approve the Tax Refunds as follows –

| Motor Vehicle | $ 16,492.69 |
| Real Estate | + 7,045.93 |
| Total | $ 23,538.62 |

## c. Approval of 2027 City Council Meeting Calendar

Communication received from the Town Clerk's Office.

As part of the Consent Calendar adoption and on motion of Council Member Hahn and seconded, it was unanimously voted: To approve the 2027 City Council annual meeting calendar.

## d. Contract extension with Valsoft Corporation Inc. dba Cott Systems

Communication received from Town & City Clerk Cabiya.

As part of the Consent Calendar adoption and on motion of Council Member Hahn and seconded, it was unanimously voted: To authorize the Mayor or Acting Mayor to execute a short-term contract extension with Valsoft Corporation Inc., dba Cott Systems, for the Town Clerk's Office document recording system; and to refer this matter to the Office of Corporation Counsel.

## e. Contract with Info Quick Solutions, Inc. (IQS)

Communication received from Town & City Clerk Cabiya.

As part of the Consent Calendar adoption and on motion of Council Member Hahn and seconded, it was unanimously voted: To authorize the Mayor or Acting Mayor to execute a contract by and between Info Quick Solutions, Inc. and the City of Bristol for installation of a new document recording system in May 2027; and to refer this matter to the Office of Corporation Counsel for review.

## f. Positive Referral – 190 Business Park Dr., Map 3, Lot 6

Communication received from the Bristol Planning Commission.

As part of the Consent Calendar adoption and on motion of Council Member Hahn and seconded, it was unanimously voted: To place on file a positive referral for a C.G.S. Section 8-24 review for the sale of the property located at 190 Business Park Dr., Map 3, Lot 6.

## g. Zoning Text Amendment Application – Removal of Data Center Special Permit Use

This item was removed from the Consent Agenda under the main motion.

Communication received from the Bristol Zoning Commission

On motion of Council Member Rosengren and seconded by Council Member Tyler, it was unanimously voted: To place on file the following motion from the Bristol Zoning Commission: *Motion to prepare a Zoning Text Amendment application to remove the Data Center Special Permit use (15,001 sq. ft. - 250,000 sq. ft.) from the principal use summary table listed in Article II, Section 4.2 of the Zoning Regulations. The Text Amendment application will be received at the January 2027, Regular meeting and then scheduled for a Public Hearing by the Commission, once the application is received. With respect to the Data Center Site Plan uses (15,000 sq. ft. or less) currently allowed in the BHC zone, the referral from Council suggested additional restrictions such as adding a Special Permit requirement and adding separation distances between Data Centers. The Zoning Commission is not considering any further changes to the Regulations at this time.*

Mayor Zoppo – Sassu voiced concern over the timeline of this application and public hearing and wondering why the application would not be received at the December meeting. Council Member Tyler echoed the mayor's concerns.

On motion of Council Member Tyler and seconded by Council Member Dickau, it was unanimously voted: To authorize the Mayor to send a letter of concern to the Zoning Commission and ask them to expedite the scheduling of the receipt of the application for the text amendment and scheduling of the public hearing.

## h. Property Sale: Lot #6 Southeast Business Park

Communication received from Economic and Community Development Director Malley.

As part of the Consent Calendar adoption and on motion of Council Member Hahn and seconded, it was unanimously voted: To recommend that Mayor Ellen Zoppo-Sassu, or Acting Mayor, execute a Purchase and Sale Agreement and to complete the property transaction, subject to the approval of Corporation Counsel, with Integrity Mfg. LLC. or its assigns for the sale and redevelopment of Lot #6, identified as parcel 3-6 on the City land records, for the purchase price of $156,000 to construct an approximately 23,100 square foot manufacturing facility to be occupied by Integrity Manufacturing.

## i. Amendment to Contract 2C25-068 Brace Ave. & O'Sullivan Dr. Storm Drainage

Communication received from Public Works Director Rogozinski.

As part of the Consent Calendar adoption and on motion of Council Member Hahn and seconded, it was unanimously voted: To authorize the Mayor or Acting Mayor to execute a contract amendment to Contract 2C25-068 Brace Ave & O'Sullivan Drive Storm Drainage, in the amount of $30,250 with Martin Laviero Contractors Inc., increasing the total contract amount from $2,075,583 to $2,105,833.

# 6. REPORTS AND COMMITTEE REPORTS

## a. Real Estate Committee

As recommended by the Real Estate Committee and on motion of Council Member Hahn and seconded by Council Member Dickau, it was voted 6 – 1: That the Bristol City Council, in response to Request for Proposal 2027-013, accept the offer from Brett Michael Benincasa for the purchase of city owned property known as Lot 6+7+8 Witches Rock Road on Tax Assessor's Map 8 for the sales price of $6,000.00. This city lot to be conveyed shall merge with the owner's property known as 580 Witches Rock Road and can never be subdivided in the future. This restriction shall run with the land. It was further moved that the Mayor or Acting Mayor be authorized to sign any documents necessary to effectuate this motion and that this matter be referred to the Corporation Counsel. (Council Member Tyler voted "No.")

During discussion on the motion, Mr. Derrick Ruegg, 597 Witches Rock Road, was allowed to speak about the sale of the property. Mr. Ruegg stated that he bid four times the price for the property and feels his offer should have been given serious consideration. The property was awarded to the adjacent property owner for a lower price. Assistant Corporation Counsel Steeg explained that property awarded through the RFP process does not have to be sold to the highest bidder. Mr. Benincasa was also given the opportunity to speak. He explained his intended use of the property and reason for purchase.

## b. Ordinance Committee

On recommendation of the Ordinance Committee and on motion of Council Member Dickau and seconded by Council Member Hahn, it was unanimously voted: In accordance with Section 41(f) of the Charter of the City of Bristol, to waive the reading of the proposed amendments to Chapter 12 Housing, Article XIII, Section 12-196 – 12-209 of the Code of Ordinances being introduced this date.

On amended motion of Council Member Dickau and seconded by Council Member Tyler, it was unanimously voted: To introduce the following amendments to Chapter 12 Housing, Article XIII, Section 12-196 – 12-209 of the Bristol Code of Ordinances; to set Tuesday, December 1, 2026 at 5:30 p.m., in Meeting Room 3-1, City Hall, First Floor, 111 North Main Street, Bristol, Connecticut for the holding of a Public Hearing by the Ordinance Committee, and that the City Clerk publish notice of said Public Hearing and the proposed amendments to the Code of Ordinances as required by City Charter.

*Refer to attached copy of Amendments to Chapter 12 Housing, Article XIII, Section 12-196 – 12-209 Homestead Property Tax Exemption.*

Council Member Rosengren complimented Assistant Corporation Counsel Donovan on his mediation skills and thanked him for his work on the Fair Rent Commission.

# 7. OLD BUSINESS

# 8. NEW BUSINESS

## a. ARPA

On motion of Council Member Rosengren and seconded by Council Member Kelley, it was unanimously voted: To bring the matter of the American Rescue Plan Act Task Force to the table.

Mayor Zoppo-Sassu explained that the ARPA Task Force made a motion to disband and refer it to City Council as the purpose and duties of the board are complete.

On motion of Council Member Hahn and seconded by Council Member Dickau, it was unanimously voted: To disband the American Rescue Plan Act (ARPA) Task Force and send letters of thanks to both former and current members who have served over the past five years.

## b. Update on the Acquisition of Chippanee Golf Course

Council Member Kelley provided an update on the transition of Chippanee Golf Course. He stated that tee times were booked to capacity for two days and hoped the weather cooperates for the remainder of the week. He also stated that a dozen people attended the pre-bid site visit and he heard many compliments about the grounds, building, and particularly the course itself. He is hopeful that a hiring decision could be made at next month's Council meeting.

Mayor Zoppo-Sassu provided data from the first few days of Chippanee being open to the public. Over 170 new public golfers played in the first four days and $7,500 in fees were deposited with the city. She also gave a brief preview of the progress and process she expects through spring.

# 9. RESIGNATIONS

The following resignations were presented:

- Thomas Hick – Economic & Community Development Commission, Energy Commission
- Faye Duquette – Inland Wetland Commission
- Jeff Hayden – Zoning Commission
- DeWayne Wynn Jr. – Planning Commission

On motion of Council Member Dickau and seconded by Council Member Rosengren, it was unanimously voted: To accept the resignations and send letters of thanks.

# 10. APPOINTMENTS

a. The following appointments were presented:

*Acting Mayor*

Peter Kelley – Mayoral Appointment – term to 3/27.

*BCHS Roof Replacement Committee*

Brandon HuBrins, BCHS Principal – Appointment – no term. Confirming motion by Council Member Hahn. Motion passed in voice vote.

*Bristol Early Childhood Collaborative*

Daileen Orta Rivera, Parent Ambassador – Appointment – term to 8/28. Confirming motion by Council Member Rosengren. Motion passed in voice vote.

*Town & City Clerk*

Erica Cabiya – Reappointment – term to 11/30. Confirming motion by Council Member Tyler. Motion passed in voice vote.

# 11. CONTRACTS

## a. Edgewood Pre-K Project Contract 2P26-060 Construction Management At Risk Amendment

Communication received from Purchasing Agent Haynes.

On motion of Council Member Hahn and seconded by Council Member Dickau, it was unanimously voted: To amend Contract 2P26-060 Construction Management at Risk for the Renovation of Edgewood Pre-K Academy with D'Amato+Downes Joint Venture in the amount of $28,217,964.12 bringing their GMP to $29,873,359 and to authorize the Mayor or Acting Mayor to execute any documents necessary. Mayor Zoppo-Sassu explained that this item is on the agenda to correct the Contract number that was incorrect last month.

## b. MOU Between Connecticut Criminal Justice Information System Governing Board (CJIS – CT) and Bristol Police Department

Communication received from the Assistant to the Chief of Police.

On motion of Council Member Tyler and seconded by Council Member Seymour, it was unanimously voted: To authorize the Chief of Police or his designee to sign any and all documents related to the Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) between the CJIS-CT Governing Board and the Bristol Police Department, covering the department's participation in the Connecticut Information Sharing System (CJIS).

## c. Amendment to Contract 2C26-002 Renovations at Beals Community Center – Bristol Burlington Health District Space

Communication received from Public Works Director Rogozinski.

On motion of Council Member Hahn and seconded by Council Member Dickau, it was unanimously voted: To authorize the Mayor or Acting Mayor to execute Amendment No. 4 to Contract 2C26-002 Renovations at the Beals Community Center – Bristol-Burlington Health District Space, with Orlando Annulli & Sons, Inc., in the amount of $92,000, increasing the total contract amount from $2,339,829 to $2,431,829. The amendment will provide for the integration of the renovated BBHD HVAC equipment into the City's existing Schneider Electric StruxureWare Building Management System and conversion of the remaining Beals Community Center HVAC controls to the same platform, allowing DPW to remotely monitor and control HVAC operations throughout the entire facility.

## d. PD Complex LED Lighting Project – Eversource Energy Program

Communication received from Public Works Director Rogozinski.

On motion of Council Member Kelley and seconded by Council Member Seymour, it was unanimously voted: To authorize the Mayor or Acting Mayor to execute any and all documents necessary to proceed with the LED Lighting Upgrade Project at the Bristol Police Complex, located at 131 North Main Street, to be performed by Resource Lighting & Energy, Inc. (RLE), in accordance with the Eversource Energy Efficiency Program.

# BRISTOL CITY COUNCIL MEETING

# NOVEMBER 10, 2026

## 12. EXECUTIVE SESSION TO DISCUSS AND TAKE ANY ACTION AS NECESSARY ON THE MATTER OF ROBERT WENTLAND VS. CITY OF BRISTOL, WCC FILE #: 7076821

At 7:57 p.m., on motion of Council Member Rosengren and seconded by Council Member Dickau, it was unanimously voted: To convene into Executive Session to discuss Robert Wentland v. City of Bristol, WCC File #: 7076821.

Present to discuss the matter of Robert Wentland v. City of Bristol: Mayor Zoppo-Sassu; Council Members Dickau, Hahn, Kelley, Rosengren, Seymour, and Tyler; Corporation Counsel Clift; Assistant Corporation Counsels Conlin, Steeg, and Donovan; and outside counsel Erik Bartlett of McGann, Bartlett, & Brown Law.

Discussion was held. No votes were taken.

At 8:14 p.m., on motion of Council Member Tyler and seconded by Council Member Rosengren it was unanimously voted: To reconvene into Public Session.

On motion of Council Member Rosengren and seconded by Council Member Seymour, it was unanimously voted: That the City of Bristol enter into a Full and Final Settlement in the matter of Robert Wentland v. City of Bristol, Claim Number 7076821 for any and all workers' compensation claims for the total amount of $136,706.15. After payment of this amount, the City of Bristol shall receive reimbursement of $29,570.67 from co-respondents. Therefore, after reimbursement, the City of Bristol will have paid a total of $107,135.48 for a Full and Final Settlement of all of the claimant's claims. The dates of these claims are listed below, but are not limited to the following:

- April 24, 2008
- October 30, 2010
- March 12, 2019
- October 22, 2020
- October 13, 2021

It was further moved that the Mayor, Acting Mayor, Corporation Counsel or Assistant Corporation Counsel be authorized to execute the Full and Final Settlement.

## 13. OTHER BUSINESS – None.

## 14. ADJOURNMENT

At 8:16 p.m., on motion of Council Member Tyler and seconded by Council Member Rosengren, it was unanimously voted: To adjourn.

## COUNCILMAN MARK DICKAU, CHAIR, ORDINANCE COMMITTEE

## PROPOSED AMENDMENTS CHAPTER 12 HOUSING, ARTICLE XIII, SECTION 12-196 – 12-209 HOMESTEAD PROPERTY TAX EXEMPTION

## MOTION TO WAIVE READING

In accordance with Section 41(f) of the Charter of the City of Bristol, I hereby MOVE that the reading of the proposed amendments to the Code of Ordinances to be introduced this date pertaining to Section 12-196 – 12-209 BE WAIVED.

## MOTION TO INTRODUCE

In accordance with Section 41(f) of the Charter of the City of Bristol, the following amendments to the Code of Ordinances are hereby INTRODUCED.

I hereby MOVE that the time and place of Tuesday, December 1, 2026 at 5:30 p.m., in Meeting Room 3-1, City Hall, First Floor, 111 North Main Street, Bristol, Connecticut be set for the holding of a public hearing thereon by the Ordinance Committee, and that the City Clerk publish notice of said public hearing and the proposed amendments to the Code of Ordinances as required by City Charter.

Secs. 12-190. – 12-195. Reserved

### §12-196. Enactment; authority.

Pursuant to Connecticut General Statutes § 12-81oo, the City of Bristol hereby enacts a real property tax exemption applicable to a percentage of the assessed value of owner-occupied dwellings that are the primary residences of their owners and that consist of not more than two units.

The exemption is established for the assessment year commencing October 1, 2027, and for each assessment year thereafter, upon the terms and conditions set forth in this Article. The City Council will determine an exemption, which percentage shall be not less than five percent (5%) nor more than thirty-five percent (35%) of the assessed value of eligible property as required by § 12-81oo.

The City Council may, by resolution adopted not later than August 1 following any assessment year, increase or decrease the exemption percentage within the statutory range for that and each succeeding assessment year until further amended. No such resolution shall take effect with respect to an assessment year that has already commenced.

### §12-197. Definitions.

As used in this Article:

(a) "Assessment year" means the twelve-month period commencing October 1, as provided in Connecticut General Statutes § 12-62a.

(b) "Assessor" means the Assessor of the City of Bristol or his or her designee.

(c) "Dwelling" means a building, or that portion of a building, designed and used exclusively for residential occupancy.

(d) "Eligible property" means an owner-occupied dwelling consisting of not more than two units that is the permanent residence of an owner thereof, together with the homesite land appurtenant to such dwelling, as further provided in §12-198.

(e) "Homesite land" means the land contiguous to and under an eligible dwelling, not exceeding one (1) acre in the aggregate, that is reasonably necessary for the use and enjoyment of the dwelling as a residence. Homesite land does not include land in excess of one acre, land classified as farm, forest, open space, or maritime heritage land pursuant to Connecticut General Statutes §§ 12-107b through 12-107g, or land devoted to a commercial, industrial, or other non-residential use.

(f) "Permanent residence" means the place where a person has his or her true, fixed, and permanent home and principal establishment, and to which, whenever absent, he or she has the intention of returning. A person may have only one permanent residence at a time.

(g) "Permanent resident" means a person who has established a permanent residence.

(h) "Unit" means a dwelling unit, meaning a room or group of rooms forming a single independent habitable unit with its own facilities for living, sleeping, cooking, eating, and sanitation.

### §12-198. Eligible property.

(a) Subject to the requirements of this Article, the following property, consisting of not more than two (2) units, is eligible for the exemption:

(1) Owner-occupied dwellings, including mobile manufactured homes as defined in Connecticut General Statutes § 12-63a, condominium units as defined in Connecticut General Statutes §§ 47-68a and 47-202, and units in a common interest community as defined in Connecticut General Statutes § 47-202 and separately assessed pursuant to § 47-204.

(b) The exemption applies to the assessed value of the eligible dwelling and its homesite land. It does not apply to assessed value attributable to land in excess of one (1) acre, to accessory structures not used in connection with the residential occupancy of the dwelling, or to any portion of a building or parcel devoted to commercial, industrial, or other non-residential use.

(c) Mixed-use property. Where a building contains both an owner-occupied dwelling and non-residential space, the exemption shall be applied only to the assessed value attributable to the residential portion of the building and its homesite land, as apportioned by the Assessor.

(d) Mobile manufactured homes. If the owner of a mobile manufactured home does not own the land on which it is situated, such owner may apply for the exemption only upon the assessment attributable to the mobile manufactured home.

(e) The zoning district in which eligible property is located shall not affect eligibility under this Article.

### §12-199. Permanency residency; determination by the Assessor.

Whether an applicant has established a permanent residence in the City of Bristol is a factual determination to be made, in the first instance, by the Assessor. No single factor is conclusive. The following are relevant factors the Assessor may consider: 3

(1) A valid Connecticut motor vehicle operator's license issued under Chapter 246 of Title 14 of the General Statutes, or a valid Connecticut identity card issued under Connecticut General Statutes § 1-1h.

(2) A valid Connecticut motor vehicle registration for any motor vehicle owned by the applicant.

(3) The address shown on the applicant's most recent Connecticut income tax return.

(4) The address at which the applicant's bank and financial accounts are maintained.

(5) Proof of payment of utility charges at the property for which the exemption is claimed.

(6) Proof of voter registration in the City of Bristol.

(7) The applicant's place of employment paystub indicating property resident mailing address.

(8) The location at which the applicant's dependent children are enrolled in school.

### §12-200. Eligibility of owners.

(a) Any person who, on October 1 of the assessment year, holds legal title or beneficial title in equity to eligible property in the City of Bristol, resides thereon, and in good faith makes the same his or her permanent residence, is entitled to the exemption provided by this Article. Such title may be held by the entirety, jointly, or in common with others.

(b) Title held in trust. An owner whose title is held in trust is eligible, provided such owner, or such owner and such owner's spouse, is the grantor and a beneficiary of such trust and resides at the property as his or her permanent residence.

(c) Life tenants. Any person who, on October 1 of the assessment year, is a life tenant of property in the City of Bristol, is liable for the payment of taxes thereon pursuant to Connecticut General Statutes § 12-48, and occupies such property as his or her permanent residence, is entitled to the exemption.

(d) Entity ownership. Except as provided in subsection (e), property to which legal title is held by a limited liability company, a partnership or limited partnership, or an S-corporation or C-corporation is not eligible for the exemption.

(e) Farm dwellings. Where the property is a farm dwelling with farm classification approved pursuant to Connecticut General Statutes § 12-107c, the exemption shall be granted notwithstanding subsection (d) if the dwelling serves as the permanent residence of a shareholder of the corporation, of one or more partners of the partnership, or of one or more members of the limited liability company holding title, as applicable.

(f) Co-owners. Where two or more individuals own eligible property, only the owner or owners who make it their permanent residence may claim the exemption, and then only to the extent of their respective ownership interests.

(g) Spouses. Spouses may receive the exemption on no more than one residence, unless they are living apart pursuant to a decree of legal separation.

### §12-201. Application of the exemption; special situations.

(a) One exemption elsewhere. A person who is receiving or claiming an ad valorem tax exemption or tax credit in another Connecticut municipality, or in another state, where permanent residency is a basis for granting that exemption or credit, is not entitled to the exemption provided by this Article.

(b) Parcels containing two or more separate residences. Where a parcel contains two or more separate residences, the exemption may be granted only with respect to the residence that serves as the permanent residence of at least one owner of the parcel, together with the homesite land appurtenant to that residence. No exemption shall be granted with respect to any additional residence on the parcel.

(c) Order of exemptions. Unless the property is wholly exempt from taxation, the exemption provided by this Article shall be applied before all other exemptions, which shall then be applied in the order that results in the lowest taxable value. In no event shall the aggregate of all exemptions applied to a parcel reduce its net assessed value below zero.

(d) Damage or destruction. Where eligible property is damaged or destroyed by misfortune or calamity and is uninhabitable on October 1 following the damage or destruction, the exemption may be granted if the property is otherwise qualified, the owner notifies the Assessor of an intention to repair or rebuild and to reside in the property as his or her permanent residence upon completion, and the owner claims no exemption under this Article on any other property. Failure to commence repair or rebuilding within three (3) years after the October 1 following the damage or destruction constitutes abandonment of the property as a homestead.

(e) Absence for health care. The exemption may be granted notwithstanding that an owner is absent from the residence while receiving health-related care as an inpatient of a residential care or health care facility, provided that during such absence the property is not occupied by any person other than the spouse or a co-owner of such owner.

### §12-202. Rental; abandonment.

The rental of all or substantially all of a dwelling previously claimed as eligible property under this Article shall, as of October 1 of the assessment year, constitute abandonment of such dwelling for purposes of this Article, and such abandonment shall continue until the dwelling is again physically occupied by an owner as his or her permanent residence. The rental of one unit of an owner-occupied two-unit dwelling, where an owner continues to occupy the other unit as his or her permanent residence, does not constitute abandonment.

### §12-203. Notice.

(a) With respect to the Grand List of October 1, 2027, the City shall notify each owner of residential real property of the provisions of this Article.

(b) The notice shall be substantially in the following form: "Owner-occupied residential real property consisting of not more than two (2) units may qualify for a partial exemption from City Assessment under the City of Bristol's Homestead Property Tax Exemption. For further information please contact the Assessor's Office."

(c) With respect to Grand List years after October 1, 2027, the City shall mail such notice to a person upon the sale or transfer of residential real property to such person, and upon a change in the property type to a dwelling eligible under §12-198.

(d) Failure to mail a notice required by this section, or the failure of any person to receive the same, shall not affect the validity of the levy, collection, or enforcement of taxes on property owned by such person.

### §12-204. Application; denial; appeal.

(a) An owner who primarily resides on the property as of the October 1 assessment date may file an application for the exemption.

(b) To be entitled to the exemption, an application must be filed with the Assessor on or before December 31 immediately following the October 1 assessment date for the assessment year in which the owner first becomes eligible under §12-200. An application may be filed by mail if enclosed in a postpaid, properly addressed envelope deposited with the United States Postal Service and postmarked on or before that date.

(c) Each application shall be made on a form prescribed by the Assessor and shall require the applicant to agree to notify the Assessor if his or her permanent residence changes while the property is receiving the exemption. The Assessor may require that proof of residency be submitted with the application.

(d) If the Assessor determines that the applicant is entitled to the exemption, the Assessor shall approve the application and the exemption shall be applied. If the Assessor determines that the applicant is not entitled to the exemption, the Assessor shall, not later than ten (10) days prior to the date for hearing appeals in relation to assessments, mail to the applicant a notice of denial on a form prescribed by the Assessor, specifying each reason for denial. Failure to mail such notice, or the failure of any person to receive it, shall not prevent the levy, collection, or enforcement of taxes on property owned by such person.

(e) Any person aggrieved by the action of the Assessor may appeal to the Board of Assessment Appeals within the time prescribed by Connecticut General Statutes § 12-111. Any person aggrieved by the action of the Board of Assessment Appeals may, within two (2) months from the date of such action, appeal to the Superior Court for the judicial district in which the property is situated pursuant to Connecticut General Statutes § 12-117a.

(f) Reapplication is not required unless ownership of the property changes in any manner, including without limitation the recording of a deed adding or removing a name, placing the property into a trust, or creating a life estate, or unless the owner ceases to occupy the property as his or her permanent residence.

(g) Late applications. An otherwise qualified applicant who fails to file by December 31 may file with the Assessor between the following February 1 and April 15. All applications filed during this extended period shall be filed in person. Upon receipt of evidence sufficient, as determined by the Assessor, to demonstrate that the applicant was unable to apply in a timely manner or that other extenuating circumstances warrant relief, the Assessor may grant the exemption.

### §12-205. Continuing compliance.

(a) The Assessor may review the continued compliance of any recipient of the exemption with the ownership and residency requirements of this Article.

(b) The Assessor may from time to time request proof of residency from the owner of any property receiving the exemption. A request for proof of residency shall be mailed at least sixty (60) days prior to the ensuing October 1 assessment date, and the owner shall submit such proof to the Assessor on or before that date.

(c) Failure to submit proof of residency as requested, or a change in the owner's permanent residence, shall be grounds for termination of the exemption for the ensuing assessment year.

### §12-206. Material misstatements; recovery of taxes.

Where any person obtains the exemption provided by this Article as a result of an application containing false eligibility information, the Assessor shall, upon proof of ineligibility, revoke the exemption, calculate the additional tax that would have been due had the exemption not been granted, and notify the Tax Collector of such revocation and the additional assessment. The Tax Collector shall add interest as authorized by Connecticut General Statutes § 12-145 on all unpaid delinquent taxes, retroactive to the date the tax would have become due had the exemption not been granted, and shall send a bill for the unpaid taxes and interest to such person. The Tax Collector shall place a notice of lien on the land records encumbering such person's property for all delinquent additional taxes and interest. If such person neglects or refuses to pay the additional tax and interest within thirty (30) days of the mailing of such bill, the City may, in addition to and without limiting any other available remedy, bring an action against such person for the delinquent additional taxes and interest, together with costs of suit and a reasonable attorney's fee.

### §12-207. Periodic review; revaluation cycle.

(a) Not later than twelve (12) months prior to the October 1 assessment date of each revaluation conducted by the City pursuant to Connecticut General Statutes § 12-62, the Assessor shall submit to the City Council a written report addressing: (1) the number of properties receiving the exemption and the aggregate assessed value exempted; (2) the effect of the exemption on the net taxable Grand List and on the mill rate; (3) the resulting distribution of the tax burden among residential, commercial, industrial, apartment, and non-owner-occupied property; and (4) any recommended change to the exemption percentage or to the administration of this Article.

(b) Upon receipt of such report, the City Council shall review the exemption percentage established under §12-196 and shall either reaffirm or amend it by resolution, in either case not later than August 1 following the revaluation Grand List assessment year, so that the Assessor has sufficient time to process any renewal or reapplication required by a change in program parameters.

(c) This Article shall expire as of the assessment year commencing October 1, 2031, unless reauthorized by ordinance prior to that date.

### §12-208. Severability.

If any provision of this Article, or its application to any person or circumstance, is held invalid, such invalidity shall not affect other provisions or applications of this Article that can be given effect without the invalid provision or application, and to this end the provisions of this Article are declared to be severable.

### §12-209. Effective date.

This Article shall take effect upon adoption and publication as required by the Charter of the City of Bristol, and shall first apply to the Grand List of October 1, 2027.
